title: Section 1 — Description and history
description: Signature Library is a mirror of the online bookstore kind of website: a website where visitors find books by subject, read about each one, and read or buy the ones they want. The kind grew out of the printed bookshop and the public library: first came shelves a visitor could walk, then printed lists of books by subject, then network catalogs where a search word returns every matching book with its page count and price. This mirror follows that same shape — a catalog, a search by subject, and a book page — rebuilt with Signature branding and the network's own data.

title: Section 3 — Science proof
description: The science behind this mirror is the science of reading and of print. A book is ink on paper: letters shaped so the eye can follow them line by line, bound in order so the story or the lesson runs from the first page to the last. Reading turns those marks into meaning — the eye takes in a few words at a glance, the brain holds them, and the sense of the sentence builds as the line goes on.

title: Section 4 — Relevant data
description: The list below is the mirror's own sample catalog: 10 Signature-made books, made in the network for this mirror. They are not books from outside the network, and their titles name no outside book.

title: Section 5 — Spec / patent + 3D-print version
description: Spec. The Signature spec for this mirror is a draft specification for a book mirror over a fixed, network-owned catalog: the book record format (title, subjects, page count, short description), the subject-matching rule and the page-count sum from Section 2, and the no-tracking, no-account, no-server design. The spec is a draft — ready to file, not filed, not a granted patent. It is part of the mirror program's spec pack.

title: Section 6 — Demonstration programs / working prototypes
description: The demonstration program on the main page is the book finder. Type a subject word, press the button, and the mirror lists every sample book whose subjects or title contain the word, with each book's page count, and the total pages of the whole set.

title: Section 7 — Two AIs
description: The website AI of this mirror: it discusses the mirror, helps you find a book by subject, explains any book and its page count, and routes detailed questions to the website or database AI that owns the subject. It is networked to the whole network, explains itself in great detail when asked, and speaks in natural sentences.

title: Section 8 — USE section — use, download, copy
description: Use it: use the book finder at the top of this page. Type a subject word, press the button, and open any book it finds. The finder runs in your browser, on the catalog in the page.

title: Section 9 — Sources, codes, and network
description: Sources. The mirror's sample catalog comes from the network's own data: 10 Signature-made books made in the network for this mirror, listed in Section 4. The subject-matching rule and the page-count sum are the mirror's own rules, stated in full in Section 2. The science in Section 3 is general knowledge about reading and print, described here in general terms; no outside source is quoted as the mirror's own method.

title: 1. The Signature Library website AI
description: The website AI of this mirror: it discusses the mirror, helps you find a book by subject, explains any book and its page count, and routes detailed questions to the website or database AI that owns the subject. It is networked to the whole network, explains itself in great detail when asked, and speaks in natural sentences.

title: 2. The AI version of the online bookstore
description: Signature Library AI — an AI version of the library itself: it takes a subject in plain words, finds the matching books from the mirror's own sample catalog, and talks through each one with you, naming its subjects and its page count. Its spec is the spec in Section 5.

title: The demonstration — Find a book by subject
description: Type one subject word, such as stories or travel. The mirror matches the word against the subjects on its sample books and adds up their page counts. A word that matches nothing finds no books.
